rules.name: 0. Let # and ~ reach the phonemizer in the app
rules.where: Sources/ReadAloud/TextPrep.swift, speechText(_:) (unchanged by fix3/reading)
rules.trigger: Today sub("[*#`~|•▪●◦]+", " ") strips every # and ~ before the phonemizer runs. Split it. Keep stripping [*`|•▪●◦]+ and any run of two or more # or ~ ("##", "~~strike~~"). Keep a single # when it's glued to a digit on either side (#1, #31#), follows a letter (C#, F#), comes before " of", or follows a key verb ((?i:press|hit|tap|dial|enter)\s#). Keep a single ~ when an optional space, sign or currency and then a digit follow it, or when it sits between two digits (9~5).
rules.reads_as: No reading of its own. It lets rules 10 and 13 and the lexicon's C# and F# entries see their symbols. Hashtags, markdown headings, ~/paths and ~~strike~~ are still stripped.
rules.risks: Without the runs rule, "Now ~~$10~~ $8" would keep the tilde before $10 and read "about ten dollars". A trailing keypad # ("#31#") must survive, or the phonemizer reads "number 31". Add chunk_cases to Tests/g2p/regression.json ("We're #1 again.", "I write C# daily.", "We need ~5 people.", "Dial #31# now.", "Now ~~$10~~ $8."), because --speech-test only runs the phonemizer.

rules.name: 1. Shorthand pass before the custom lexicon
rules.where: Sources/Phonemizer/Phonemizer.swift phonemize(): new TextNormalizer.shorthand(t) after linkLabels/foldMicroSign and before custom.mark (only when normalizes)
rules.trigger: Holds rules 2–5 (the slash shorthands and Attn) and 7 (min./max.).
rules.reads_as: Ordering requirement only.
rules.risks: Needed because (1) "Max" is a case-sensitive tech-lexicon key, so "Max. 3 per customer" is marked [Max](/mˈæks/) before TextNormalizer runs, and TextNormalizer skips marked spans; and (2) CustomLexicon never matches right after "/", so "w/Kubernetes" reads wkjˈubəɹnˌits unless w/ is expanded first. This pass sees raw text, before the keyboard-shortcut rule that fix3/reading added, so it must keep "Shift+W/Shift+S" out on its own (rule 2's left context).

rules.name: 2. w/ family → with / without / within
rules.where: TextNormalizer.shorthand (rule 1)
rules.trigger: Left context for every form: start of text, whitespace, an opening bracket or a quote, (?<=^|[\s(\[{"“‘']). This replaces the reviewed negative lookbehind (?<![\p{L}\p{N}/.:_@\-]), which let "Shift+W/Shift+S" through as "Shift plus with Shift". Never after a number or % and a space ((?<![\d%]\s)), so "5 W/m²" and "5% w/w" stay. Then, in order: (a) ([Ww])/(out|OUT) and ([Ww])/([Oo]) → without, only when whitespace and then a letter, quote or bracket follow and the next word isn't a month or weekday name ("W/O 4512" is a work order, "w/o Jan 6" is week of). (b) ([Ww])/(in|IN) → within, before whitespace and a letter or digit. (c) Generic ([Ww])/ → with, when whitespace and then [\p{L}\p{N}$£€("“'] follow, or when it's glued to a word of two or more letters that isn't a unit (kg, km, cm, mm, m², hr, sr…). Add a space when glued. Reject the glued form when its run contains "/", "=", "?" or "." plus a letter (w/index.php).
rules.reads_as: "with", "without", "within". "With" when the shorthand starts a sentence or line ("W/ love, Mia"). "WITH" or "WITHOUT" when the next word is all capitals (two or more letters), so a shouted menu line stays shouted for unshout.
rules.risks: Single-letter pairs stay because the generic form needs whitespace or a word of two or more letters: w/e, w/c, w/w, W/L, W/D (frozen). URLs and paths (/w/, example.com/w/page) fail the left-context check. Watts per unit (W/kg, W/m²) are blocked by the number check and the unit list.

rules.name: 3. b/c → because
rules.where: TextNormalizer.shorthand (rule 1)
rules.trigger: Same left context as rule 2. ([bB])/c with a lower-case c, (?![\p{L}\p{N}/]|\.\p{L}). Not after an operator ([=+\-*×÷^/<>] and an optional space before the left-context space). It must be followed by whitespace and a word other than is, are, was, were, equals, and or or, and not by "=" or ")".
rules.reads_as: "because", or "Because" when written "B/c".
rules.risks: Maths was the gap in the reviewed trigger: "Let x = a + b/c" and "The ratio b/c is small" would have read "because" (both frozen now). All-caps B/C (hepatitis B/C, benefit/cost) is untouched. Paths (a/b/c, example.com/b/c) fail the left-context check.

rules.name: 4. c/o → care of
rules.where: TextNormalizer.shorthand (rule 1)
rules.trigger: Same left context as rule 2. ([Cc])/([Oo])(?=\s+\p{Lu}): only before a capitalised word (a name or company), never before ":", a digit or #.
rules.reads_as: "care of" ("Care of" at the start of a line).
rules.risks: Clinical "c/o chest pain" and "C/O: Chest pain" (colon), and hotel "C/O 11 AM", are untouched (frozen). The remaining risk is C/O meaning check-out or change order before a capitalised word ("C/O Time", "C/O Request"), which is rare in prose.

rules.name: 5. Attn → Attention
rules.where: TextNormalizer.shorthand (rule 1); Tokenizer.titleContinues/runOnTitles for the sentence split
rules.trigger: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.])(Attn|ATTN|attn)(?:\.(?=\s|$)|(?=\s*:)|(?=\s+\p{Lu})): with a colon or a period, or bare before a capitalised word. Also join "Attn." before a capital in Tokenizer.titleContinues, because NLTokenizer splits "Attn." | "Maria Lopez" (re-checked with a compiled probe).
rules.reads_as: "Attention". A following ":" stays as the pause and the abbreviation point is dropped. "ATTENTION" when the next word is all caps.
rules.risks: Lower-case attn before a lower-case word ("the attn weights", self.attn) is untouched (frozen).

rules.name: 6. est. → established / estimated
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules, next to the abbreviations loop
rules.trigger: The period is required; bare EST and est are never touched. (a) Founding year: (Est|est)\.\s+(?:in\s+)?(1\d{3}|20\d{2})(?![\d,.]\d), followed by the end of the text, punctuation, or one of in, by, at, on, and, as, since or from → "established". All-caps EST. takes only this form, only at the start of a line or after ",", "·", "|" or "—" (sign style), and never after a clock time. (b) Amount: otherwise, est. before [~≈]?[-−]?[$£€¥₹₩]?\d → "estimated" ("est. 1500 attendees", "est. 3-5 days", "est. £2,000"). (c) Noun: est. before a word on a short list (cost, costs, delivery, arrival, time, reading, total, value, price, wait, completion, date, budget, savings, population, duration, departure, shipping, tax, payment, revenue, attendance) → "estimated". Everything else is left alone.
rules.reads_as: "established" or "estimated", capitalised to match. The number stays as digits for the number reader.
rules.risks: The reviewed form (c) (est. before any lower-case word) read the noun estimate as "estimated": "Call for a free est. today" and "The est. was too low" (frozen). The list turns those into misses that read "est". "Times are in EST. 2025 dates follow" stays the time zone, because caps EST. isn't at the start of a line and the year is followed by a noun.

rules.name: 7. min. / max. → minimum / maximum
rules.where: TextNormalizer.shorthand (rule 1): must run before custom.mark because of the "Max" lexicon key
rules.trigger: The period is required. Never after a digit (with an optional space), and never after a number word or quantifier: a, an, one … twenty, thirty … ninety, hundred, few, several, couple, many, more, some. Lower case: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.])(min|max)\.(?=\s*[~≈]?[$£€¥₹₩]?\d|\s+\p{Ll}). Capitalised (Min|Max)\. takes the same lookahead, but only at the start of a line or the text, or after "(".
rules.reads_as: "minimum" or "maximum" (capitalised to match), with the period dropped.
rules.risks: The reviewed trigger also took a capitalised Max. after ":" or ",", and min. after number words. "Assigned to: Max. 2 tickets are open" and "a ten min. walk" would have become maximum and minimum (frozen, with "a few min. with news" and "a min. let me check"). The misses read "max three", which is still natural speech.

rules.name: 8. avg, approx, excl., misc. → words
rules.where: TextNormalizer.abbreviations for the forms with a period; a small rule for the bare forms
rules.trigger: Add ("avg.","average"), ("Avg.","Average"), ("excl.","excluding"), ("Excl.","Excluding"), ("misc.","miscellaneous") and ("Misc.","Miscellaneous") to `abbreviations`. Bare forms: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.])(avg|Avg)(?![\p{L}\p{N}_(.]) → average, and (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.])(approx|Approx)(?=\s+[~≈]?[-−]?[$£€¥₹₩]?\d) → approximately.
rules.reads_as: average, excluding, miscellaneous, approximately.
rules.risks: AVG (the antivirus, SQL) and avg( in code are untouched. NLTokenizer splits "excl. VAT" before the capital, but the abbreviation still reads at the end of its chunk (the lookahead accepts $). A sentence-final "misc." should keep its full stop.

rules.name: 9. ca. / c. → circa before a year
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules (coordinate with the dates area); Tokenizer.titleContinues
rules.trigger: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.])ca\.\s?(?=\d{3,4}(?![\d,])), and lower-case only (?<![\p{L}\p{N}_.&])c\.\s?(?=(?:1\d{3}|20\d{2})(?![\d,.]\d)) → "circa ". Join "ca." or "c." before a digit in Tokenizer.titleContinues, because NLTokenizer splits "built ca." | "1850.".
rules.reads_as: "circa" followed by the year.
rules.risks: A capital "C." (an initial) is never touched. "c." before a number that isn't a year (UK statute "1998 c. 42") is untouched (frozen).

rules.name: 10. ~ → about; digit~digit → to
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules: the range form first, then the about form, both before the range and units rules
rules.reads_as: "about 5", "about $5", "about 50%", "about 1,000" (today the tilde breaks the thousands comma: "one zero zero zero"), "about -5°C", "about 5-10" (then "5 to 10"), and "9~5" → "9 to 5".
rules.risks: Semver "~4.17.21" was a gap in the reviewed trigger (frozen; the dotted-version lookahead skips it). ~/Documents, ~y, "x ~ N(0,1)" and ~~strike~~ are untouched. A bitwise ~0 in code would read "about zero", which is rare. Depends on rule 0 in the app.

rules.name: 11. Glued maths symbol before a decimal (already landed)
rules.where: No new code: fixed in fix3/reading (merged b06b926)
rules.trigger: None. Since the 14:59 build, "±0.5" and "≈0.5" keep "point".
rules.reads_as: "plus or minus zero point five".
rules.risks: None. The two cases stay as regression guards.

rules.name: 12. Number signs: №, N°, Nº, Nos.; no. as the word after said
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules for №, N°, Nº and Nos.; Tokenizer.split (numberSign) for lower-case no.
rules.trigger: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}])(?:№|[Nn][°º])\s?(?=\d) → "number ". It must run before Lexicon's compatibility mapping turns № into "No". (?<![\p{L}.])(Nos|nos)\.(?=\s?#?\d) → "numbers". Lower-case "no." before a number is the word, with its full stop, only when the previous word is said, say, says, saying, answered or replied. NLTokenizer doesn't split "said no. 2 days", so this belongs in the tokenizer.
rules.reads_as: "number 5", "numbers 3 and 4", and "She said no. Two days later…".
rules.risks: The reviewed list also had was, is, were and just, which would turn "The winner is no. 3 on the list" into "no. Three" (frozen). "40°N" has a digit before the ° and isn't N°.

rules.name: 13. # → number (and the key)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules (depends on rule 0 in the app)
rules.trigger: Number: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}#&/;])#(?=\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?(?![\p{L}\d#*])) → "number ". Exceptions: CSS greys (#000 to #999, three identical digits), hex colours, keypad codes (# after the digits, "#31#"), and a # right after "No. ", "Nos. " or "no. ". Of: (?<![\p{L}\p{N}#])#(?=\s+of\b) → "number". It runs before the key rule. Key: (?<=\b(?i:press|hit|tap|dial|enter)\s)#(?=\s|[.,;:!?)]|$), not before " of" → "pound" (US) or "hash" (GB). This needs `british` passed into TextNormalizer.normalize.
rules.reads_as: "number 12", "number of", "press pound" or "press hash".
rules.risks: The reviewed trigger only checked for hex letters, so "#2020Vision" read "number 2020 Vision" (frozen now: the digits must not run into letters). "Enter # of guests" must read "number of", not "pound of". Hashtags, C#/F#, {, #! and headings are untouched. "Apt #4B" is an accepted miss.

rules.name: 14. § and ¶ (landed; one fix)
rules.where: TextNormalizer.rules: the (§§?|¶)\s? rule from fix3/reading
rules.trigger: fix3/reading already reads §, §§ and ¶, and all § cases pass. Narrow ¶: ¶¶?\s?(?=\d) → "paragraph " or "paragraphs ". Any other ¶ → "", and drop a space before it.
rules.reads_as: "section 12", "sections 12 to 14", "paragraph 4". A trailing pilcrow is silent.
rules.risks: Today "This is the end.¶" reads "…end. paragraph" (that speech case fails).

rules.name: 15. ©, (c), ™, ℠, ®
rules.where: Lexicon.symbols (fix3/reading added © → copyright, ® → registered, ™ → trademark) and TextNormalizer.rules
rules.trigger: (1) ™, ℠ and ® are silent anywhere: take them out of Lexicon.symbols and drop them in TextNormalizer, keeping a full stop that follows ("Buy Acme®."). (2) © is silent when the word copyright is next to it on either side ((?i:copyright)\s*© and ©\s*(?:\p{Lu}\p{L}*\s+)?(?i:copyright)); otherwise it stays "copyright". (3) "Copyright (c)" drops the "(c)". At the start of a line, (c) plus a year followed by the end of the line or a capitalised word → "Copyright".

open_questions: Trademark signs: the reading fixes merged today (fix3/reading, b06b926) put ™ → "trademark" and ® → "registered" back into Lexicon.symbols (Aloud 1.5's readings). Core's brief and this test set say they're silent. These two choices conflict. Should "Acme™ makes it." read "Acme makes it" (silent, recommended, because nobody reads the sign aloud) or "Acme trademark makes it"? © stays spoken ("copyright") either way. Three speech cases fail until this is settled.

Hyphenated number words: the brief writes them with hyphens ("four ninety-nine"), but the stack reads "ninety-nine" as one word (nˈIndinˌIn) while the number reader gives two (nˈIndi nˈIn). A correct reading then fails the test; the core-readings money cases fail for this reason alone. Should SpeechTest.loose fold hyphens between number words (recommended, so authors can write numbers naturally), or must every area write them unhyphenated? This set is unhyphenated. Spelled letters have the same problem ("pee em" in the core M&Ms case against the stack's single pˌiˈɛm).
Should "+" between ordinary words ("salt + pepper") be read "plus" (today) or "and"? I moved this case to frozen because both readings are natural. I recommend keeping "plus", the symbol's name.
N/A: keep the letters "N A" (today), or say "not applicable"? I recommend the letters. N/A also means "not available", so expanding it would be a guess.
"Press #": should US voices say "pound" and British voices "hash", as phone menus in each country do? I recommend yes. "#1" reads "number one" in both.
b/w: leave it as the letters "B W"? I recommend yes. It means both "between" and "black and white", and Core doesn't guess.
Should "ca." and "c." before a year be read "circa" in Core, or be left to a dates or history pack? I recommend Core, limited to lower case with a year straight after.
"5‰": read "five per mille" (as briefed) or the plainer "five per thousand"? I recommend "per mille".
review_notes: Verification: I checked every case against the shipped binary in both voices. While I was working, the binary was rebuilt at 14:59 after fix3/reading was merged (b06b926), so I re-ran everything on that build. For each case I applied the proposed rules by hand (digits kept) and compared the result with the plain-words reading using SpeechTest.loose: 0 mismatches over 179 voice runs. A script check of the hard rules found no digits, symbols, abbreviations or Roman numerals in any "says". I read the phonemes of every "says" (Kubernetes, circa, Miscellaneous, per mille, Mister, Crown copyright and hash in the British voice all come out right). 18 of the 90 speech cases pass today.
Cases that now pass because of fix3/reading: the §, §§ and ¶ 4 cases, © 2024, Photo ©, ±0.5 and ≈0.5. The reviewed rules 11 and 14 are mostly already done, and their notes say so.

New failures in the current build, each with a case: "end.¶" reads "paragraph"; "Copyright © 2024" reads copyright twice; "© Crown copyright" also reads copyright twice; "Acme™" reads "trademark"; "Kleenex®" reads "registered"; "iPhone™" becomes one word, "iPhonetrademark"; "Buy Acme®." reads "Acme registered".

Corrected speech cases: "BURGER W/ CHEESE" now says "BURGER WITH CHEESE", so the rest of the sentence matches the text. "See Nos. 3-4" became "See Nos. 3 and 4", because a two-item range is read either "three and four" or "three to four". "salt + pepper" moved to frozen, because "plus" and "and" are both natural. "Kleenex® tissues" moved from frozen to speech, because the current build reads "registered". In the "She said no." case, the old after-text hid that the fix belongs in the tokenizer. Notes are updated for the new build.

Removed 10 near-duplicate speech cases to keep the set close to the target size; none of them passed today, and each trigger is still covered. They were: Est. reading time, Growth of ~5%, Min. order $25, Price: ~£10, Read ¶¶ 4–6, Results (avg. 72), Room #12 (its TextPrep note moved to the #2 pencil case), Salt content 35 ‰, The #1 seed, and the old Nos. 3-4. Added 21 positives from emails, menus, chat, shop pages, licence headers and UK footers: Lunch w/ Sam @ noon, W/ love Mia, Reply w/in 5 days, Running late b/c of traffic, Jane Doe c/o Acme Books, Attn: Mr. Lee, Shipping est. 3-5 days, Avg. rating 4.5 stars, the min. and max. pair, Ready in 5 min. or less (a guard), ~50% off, ~1,000 (today read "one zero zero zero"), ~-5°C (British voice), A #1 New York Times bestseller, Tip #5, Enter # of guests, No. 10 Downing Street, Copyright (c) 2024, © Crown copyright 2024, Kleenex®, and Nos. 3 and 4.

Attacking the rules found 25 new near-miss frozen cases. Each one breaks a trigger as it was written. w/: Shift+W/Shift+S (+ before W/), w/w, W/L, and W/O 4512 (a work order). b/c: "a + b/c" and "the ratio b/c is small" (maths), and hepatitis B/C. c/o: "C/O: Chest pain" and "C/O 11 AM". Attn: "attn weights". est.: "a free est. today" and "The est. was too low" (the noun estimate), and "in EST. 2025 dates". max.: "Assigned to: Max. 2 tickets" (a name after a colon). min.: "a ten min. walk", "a few min. with news" and "a min. let me check". c.: "1998 c. 42" (a statute). ~: "~4.17.21" (semver). #: #2020Vision. no.: "The winner is no. 3". (c): "(c) 2019 sales rose". Also "(R)", A+ and "# Getting started". I removed 14 frozen duplicates or trivial cases. One of them, a Ctrl+W/Cmd+W case, was replaced because its reading is garbled today and would break with keyboard work.

Rule changes: rules 2–4 use a positive left context (whitespace, a bracket or a quote, or the start) instead of the old lookbehind list. w/o and w/out skip digits, months and weekdays. b/c skips maths context. est. form (c) uses a list of nouns. min. and max. skip number words and quantifiers, and the capitalised form is limited to the start of a line or after "(". no.-as-the-word applies only after said and its forms. # needs its digits not to run into letters, and the "of" reading comes before the key reading. ~ skips dotted versions. Rule 0 always strips runs of # or ~ and keeps a keypad #. © is silent next to the word copyright. A pilcrow is read only before a number.

Apple's sentence splitter: I re-checked it with my own probe (nlt/split.swift, which reads from stdin). It splits after "Attn." and "ca." before the next word, and after "excl." before a capital ("excl. VAT"). It doesn't split "said no. 2 days", "c. 1650", "est.", "Min.", "Max.", "avg." or "Nos.".

Spotted outside my area: (1) The British voice reads 2009 as "two thousand nine", but British speakers say "two thousand and nine" (numbers area), so I avoided 2000s years. (2) "40°N" reads "forty N" with no "degrees". (3) In "20 min. at" and "5 min. or less", the period after min. becomes a mid-sentence full stop (units area). (4) "A&B Plumbing" still reads A as the article. (5) e.g. still reads "E G" (the tech lexicon beats TextNormalizer). (6) TextPrep is unchanged, so the app still strips # and ~ (rule 0).
